title: Context and memory in an agent

items.stem: Your makerspace assistant is about to make one model call. Which description of its context window for that call is correct?

options.text: Only the student's latest message, since the model handles one message at a time
Everything sent in the call: system prompt, tool definitions, messages, tool results
The model's training data plus the student's latest message and its reply
All past conversations with every student, which the model stores itself

items.stem: In a five-step agent loop, the fifth model call needs to know what the tool returned in step two. How does the model get that information?

options.text: It carries the step-two result inside itself between calls, like a running memory
It looks the result up in the tool's own log, which the model can read directly
The program includes the earlier steps in the input it sends with the fifth call
It guesses the result from its training, which usually matches what the tool returned

items.stem: In a retrieval setup over the machine manuals, what actually happens when the assistant answers a question?

options.text: A program or tool picks relevant pages and puts them into the context for the model
The model already knows where each page is and reads it straight from storage
The model's weights are updated with the manual so it remembers the pages later
The whole manual is loaded each time and the model ignores the irrelevant parts

items.stem: A 300-page manual fits in the window. Your team proposes pasting it into the context for every request, and a typical request takes six model calls. Which is the strongest reason this is a poor design for your small budget?

options.text: The manual would be permanently deleted from the model once the window fills
The model can only read the first page of text placed in its context
The model would refuse any input longer than a single chat message
Every call re-sends and pays for those tokens, and recall can get worse

items.stem: Which statement correctly tells apart compaction and structured notes in an agent?

options.text: Compaction saves facts to a file between sessions; notes summarize a conversation inside the model
Both happen automatically inside the model, so the program never has to store anything
Compaction summarizes a near-full conversation into a new window; notes are saved outside the window
Both only delete old messages, and neither one keeps any information from them
